name: EvolveR

paper.title: EvolveR: Self-Evolving LLM Agents through an Experience-Driven Lifecycle

construction.unit: principle: one-sentence guiding or cautionary advice + (subject, predicate, object) triples, with usage/success counts and links to up to 3 successful and 2 failed source trajectories
construction.kept_as: LLM-distilled advice; source trajectories kept verbatim in a separate store
construction.processing: the agent's own policy model distils each stored RL trajectory (question, golden answer and dialogue, cut at 4,096 characters) into a principle, with separate prompts for successes and failures
construction.writer: the policy model being trained (Qwen2.5-0.5B to 7B); GPT-4o-mini in the teacher-distill ablation

organization.stores: Milvus collections: principles (embedded) and trajectories (by id)
organization.index: BGE-M3 dense embedding of the principle description, cosine, FLAT index

management.operations: LLM pairwise dedup among new principles from the same question; match against top-3 existing (cosine >= 0.85, then LLM yes/no): link the trajectory to the match or add a new principle
management.forgetting: score = (successes+1)/(uses+2); principles below 0.3 deleted every 10 RL steps

retrieval.query: a query the agent writes inside <search_experience>, not the question itself
retrieval.selection: top-3 by similarity; duplicates and malformed principles dropped
retrieval.budget: 3 principles per call, character budget of 2,048 (max_obs_length)

use.context: type, metric score, description and triples of each principle, inside <experience> tags in the agent's own reasoning trace
use.reasoning: multi-turn think / search_experience / search_knowledge / answer loop, up to 10 turns; policy trained with GRPO to use it

classify.note: Consolidate (merge a new principle into a matching one) was chosen over evict; score-based pruning also runs. The agent decides when and with what text to search, but a fixed top-3 rule decides what comes back.

stages.ingestion: During GRPO training (8 rollouts per question), 2 of the 8 trajectories per question (1 success and 1 failure when possible) are buffered after each step.
stages.construction: After each RL step the frozen policy model distils each buffered trajectory into a principle: a one-sentence description plus structured triples, typed guiding (success) or cautionary (failure).
stages.organization: Principles form a flat pool in Milvus, indexed by a BGE-M3 embedding of the description; each keeps counters and links to up to 3 successful and 2 failed trajectory ids.
stages.update: New principles from the same question are deduplicated by pairwise LLM judgement; each survivor is compared with its top-3 neighbours (cosine >= 0.85, then LLM yes/no) and either linked to the match or added with score 0.5. Scores (successes+1)/(uses+2) are refreshed from trajectory outcomes, and principles under 0.3 are pruned every 10 steps.
stages.retrieval: The agent may emit <search_experience> with its own query at any turn; the top-3 principles by cosine are returned.
stages.answer: The agent reads the returned principles (type, score, description, triples) in <experience> tags, may also search Wikipedia, and answers in <answer> tags.
stages.learning: The policy is trained with GRPO on outcome (exact match) plus a 0.1-weighted format reward, after a cold-start SFT; retrieved experience and document tokens are masked from the loss.

summary: The agent's own policy distils its RL trajectories into scored principles that it can search as a tool during rollouts, and GRPO trains it to use them; the principle pool is deduplicated, merged and pruned by success rate.
notes: VENUE: ICML 2026 poster (icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/65641), listed there under the title 'From Interactions to Principles: Experience-Driven Self-Distillation for Evolving LLM Agents'; same authors, arXiv comment 'Accepted by ICML 2026'. Paper read: arXiv v3 (16 May 2026). CODE: the paper links github.com/Edaizi/EvolveR, which redirects to KnowledgeXLab/EvolveR; both give the same HEAD. RESULTS: all baseline numbers in Table 1 equal Search-R1 (2503.09516v5) Table 2; run_by left null because the paper does not say they were copied. DESIGN: 'offline' here means between RL steps; test-time evaluation in the code does not add trajectories, so the pool is frozen at test time.

sources.code_note: HEAD of the official repo (2026-05-08, 19 commits), a week after the ICML acceptance note in its README; the repo has no tags, so this is taken as the release behind the v3 paper. Training scripts are given for 3B only.

headline: Memory is written by the same small model that is being trained with RL, and the RL loop teaches it when to search that memory.
What reaches the agent is only the principle text, its type, its score and triples; the linked past trajectories are stored but switched off in the released scripts.
All baselines are the numbers printed in Search-R1; the 7B table leaves out Search-R1-base, which averages higher (0.431) than EvolveR (0.417).

open_questions: How much of the gain is RL versus memory? RL alone gives 0.325 and the full system 0.382 on 3B, but the memory-only (no RL) run is still 0.357 (Table 4); the baselines are not retrained with the same cold start.
The experience base is built from the NQ and HotpotQA training questions that are also in-domain test sets; the paper does not measure overlap between principles and test questions.
Scores rise with pool size up to 45k principles and then drop (Table 7), measured on a 10% validation subset while training continues, so pool size and training step are confounded.

discussion.takeaway: An agent can distil its own RL trajectories into short scored principles and learn, through RL, to search them; on seven QA benchmarks this beats the Search-R1 numbers it compares against at 3B and 7B.

claims.claim: EvolveR outperforms prompting, SFT and RL search-agent baselines.
claims.evidence: Average EM 0.382 (3B) vs 0.325 for Search-R1-instruct and 0.303 for Search-R1-base; 0.417 (7B) vs 0.385 for Search-R1-instruct. Table 1, §4.2

claims.claim: Access to the experience base at test time matters.
claims.evidence: 3B drops from 0.382 to 0.340 without experience search; 1.5B from 0.270 to 0.123. Table 3, §5.2.2

claims.claim: Self-distillation beats a stronger external distiller at 3B.
claims.evidence: 0.382 self vs 0.370 with GPT-4o-mini at 3B, but GPT-4o-mini wins at 0.5B (0.220 vs 0.150) and 1.5B (0.290 vs 0.270). Table 2, §5.2.1

claims.claim: Scoring and pruning keep useful principles.
claims.evidence: In 100 hand-labelled principles, 82% of high-score ones are ideal vs 26% of low-score ones. Table 6, §5.3
Latency 0.20 s and EM 0.387 at 49,934 principles. Table 7

limits: Principle quality is bounded by the base model's ability to distil.
Only QA tasks were tested; embodied or creative tasks remain open.
Keeping a growing experience base efficient for lifelong agents is unsolved.
A self-evolving agent could learn undesirable strategies without a value-aligned reward.
reading: Every baseline number equals Search-R1's Table 2; the 7B block drops Search-R1-base (0.431 average), which is higher than EvolveR 7B (0.417) and higher on 5 of the 7 datasets.
The retrieval query is text the agent writes, not the question; in the paper's example it is a list of guessed triples.
Past trajectories are linked to principles but never shown to the agent in the released scripts; only the one-line principle, its triples, type and score are.
The agent sees each principle's success score, so the score acts both as a pruning rule and as a signal inside the prompt.
Only 2 of 8 rollouts per question are distilled, usually one success and one failure; since in-batch dedup compares principles from the same question and same type, it has few pairs to check.
The pruning threshold barely matters (0.265 to 0.276 average over 0.1 to 0.9 on 1.5B, Table 9), so the reported score-tier quality difference (Table 6) does not translate into accuracy there.
The code gives the distiller the golden answer along with the trajectory, which the paper does not mention.

abstract.text: EvolveR lets an LLM agent improve from its own experience in a closed loop. Between RL steps, the agent's own model turns its recent trajectories into short guiding or cautionary principles, which are deduplicated, merged with near-identical ones and scored by how often they led to correct answers. During rollouts the agent can search this pool as a tool alongside a Wikipedia search, and GRPO trains it to make use of what it retrieves. On seven question-answering benchmarks with Qwen2.5 models, the authors report higher exact match than prompting, SFT and RL search-agent baselines.
